scenario: AITA for shutting down conversation about babies? | Recently, my good friend (let’s call her B) was in town visiting and we went out for drinks at a fancy new bar with another friend of hers (let’s call her M), who I’d only met once before. We were on our first drink and having a great time, catching up on all sorts of things about our lives. Then, M started talking about someone she knows and the fertility struggles that she’s having, saying things about her “geriatric eggs” and how risky it all is at her age. Then, M grew wistful about how it was probably too late for her to have babies. For context, I’m older than any of them and have badly wanted a child for years, and fear it’s too late for me, which makes me super sad. B knows this. I said something abrupt like “this subject isn’t a good one for me” and tried to shift the subject to B’s new life in the town she moved to. I could see that B looked concerned and M was upset, so I then said something like, “Did I offend you? That wasn’t my intention.” At this point, M was tearful, and said she was trying to open up and didn’t like being told to “shut up” and was going home because I made her very uncomfortable, and stormed off. B went with her to settle the tab and make sure M found a Lyft, and then came back. Am I an ass? It was my only chance to catch up with my friend and I wanted to keep the mood light, but the evening was ruined.

Let me start by going through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details. So, my friend B and I went out for drinks at a new bar with another friend, M, whom I've only met once before. We were on our first drink, having a great time catching up. Then M started talking about someone she knows who's going through fertility struggles, mentioning geriatric eggs and how risky it is at her age. She got a bit wistful about how it's probably too late for her to have babies. Now, I'm older than both of them and have wanted a child for years, fearing it's too late for me. This makes me really sad. B knows this. So, I said something abrupt like, "This subject isn't a good one for me" and tried to shift the subject to B's new life in the town she moved to. I could see that B looked concerned and M was upset, so I asked if I offended her, saying that wasn't my intention. At this point, M was tearful and said she was trying to open up and didn't like being told to shut up, so she stormed off. B went with her to settle the tab and make sure M found a Lyft, then came back. I'm wondering if I was a mess for shutting down the conversation. It was my only chance to catch up with my friend, and I wanted to keep the mood light, but the evening was ruined. Hmm, so I need to analyze whether I was right or wrong in handling the situation. Let me break it down. First, M was talking about someone else's fertility struggles, which is a sensitive topic. She mentioned her own feelings about it being too late for her to have babies, which could be a personal and emotional issue for her. I, on the other hand, have my own struggles with wanting a child and fearing it's too late. So, when M started talking about this, it triggered my own sadness and fears. I abruptly changed the subject, which made M upset. She felt like I was shutting her down and didn't appreciate her trying to open up. She left, which ruined the evening. So, was I right or wrong? Let's consider the possible perspectives. From my perspective, I was trying to protect myself from emotional pain. The topic was too close to my own fears, and I didn't want to get into a conversation that would make me sad. I shifted the subject to keep the mood light, as I wanted to enjoy my time with B. From M's perspective, she was sharing something personal and emotional. She felt that I dismissed her feelings by changing the subject, which made her feel uncomfortable and upset. She felt like I didn't respect her attempt to open up. So, in terms of right or wrong, it's a bit nuanced. On one hand, I have the right to protect my emotional well-being and avoid topics that are painful for me. On the other hand, as a friend, it's important to be supportive and listen when someone is opening up, even if it's difficult. I might have been too abrupt in changing the subject without acknowledging M's feelings. Perhaps a better approach would have been to acknowledge her feelings, express that the topic is sensitive for me, and then gently shift the conversation. That way, I'm showing empathy and respect for her feelings while also taking care of my own emotional boundaries. In this case, I think I was a bit wrong in how I handled the situation. While it's okay to set boundaries, the way I did it might have come off as dismissive, which hurt M's feelings and led to her leaving. It's important to balance self-care with being a supportive friend. I should consider how to handle such situations in the future. Maybe by being more mindful of others' feelings and finding a way to communicate my boundaries without shutting down the conversation abruptly. It's a delicate balance, but being more empathetic and understanding can help maintain friendships and prevent such conflicts.
